title: Planted q-Ary Partner-Survival Frontier and Conditional Source-Geometry Obligations

theorems.name: Support-Only Cube Survival Law
theorems.statement: For any planted ternary vector u in {-1, 0, 1}^n \ {0} with Hamming support s = supp(u) = ||u||_1 in {1, ..., n} and any dyadic cube width W >= 2, the cube-boundary survival factor in offset_average_pair_mass equals P_cube(W, u) = (1 - 1/W)^s and satisfies 1 - s/W <= P_cube(W, u) <= 1 / (1 + s/W).

theorems.name: Worst-Case Multiplicative and Additive Box Survival Bounds
theorems.statement: In the public centered-RREF kernel basis B with free support s_F = supp_F(u) and deterministic splitting (p_split = nextprime(W), g_res = 1) on a hitting free coordinate j_coord = m + j_0, the partner box difference delta satisfies P_box(M_box, delta) >= P_box^min(M_box, m, s_F) := (1 - 1/M_box)^(s_F - 1) * (1 - B_tern(s_F)/M_box)^m >= 1 - L_box(m, s_F) / M_box, where L_box(m, s_F) = (s_F - 1) + m * B_tern(s_F).

theorems.name: Modulus-Independent Dyadic (M_box, W) Schedule for the 1/ell Budget
theorems.statement: The dyadic schedule bounds intended partner failure 1-P_box*P_cube by 1/ell independently of q. This is a DCP bad-register bound only under independently established at-most-two/common-partner geometry, with fresh uniform offsets and a hitting free-coordinate trial. Neither the geometry nor a public hitting-coordinate selector follows from partner survival.

theorems.name: Conditional Integer-Cube Separation and Unconditional-Transfer Counterexample
theorems.statement: Same-cell integer differences have squared norm at most n*(W-1)^2. A verified lower bound L>n*(W-1)^2 on every nonparallel lattice vector, a primitive ternary hidden vector, a hitting free-coordinate trial, and prime p with p-1>=W suffice to exclude all unintended differences. The inequalities do not certify the lower bound. The public kernel of H=(1,1,1) over q=3 supplies a same-colour collision even when the partner-failure schedule passes.
